text.title: Poetry Project Setup — Core Rules
text.summary: 11 testable rules every python-poetry-setup application must obey — five on project shape, six on reproducibility in CI and Docker.

rule.statement: Use PEP 621 [project] table as the source of truth for name, version, dependencies, requires-python. Use [tool.poetry] only for Poetry-specific extensions.
rule.rationale: PEP 621 is the canonical metadata location; staying in it keeps the project portable between Poetry, uv, hatch, pdm.

rule.statement: poetry.lock is committed to the repo. CI installs from the lockfile.
rule.rationale: Without a committed lockfile every install resolves differently; reproducibility is gone.

rule.statement: Split dependencies into groups — main, dev, test, docs — with docs marked `optional = true`. Never mix dev tools (pytest, ruff, mypy) into runtime dependencies.
rule.rationale: Runtime install must stay slim; mixing groups bloats production containers and drags every deploy. An optional docs group keeps mkdocs out of both the runtime and the test install.

rule.statement: For libraries (publishable to PyPI): use lower-bound only constraints (>=2.0,<3) instead of caret (^2.0). For applications: caret is acceptable.
rule.rationale: Caret on libraries forces downstream users into narrow version ranges; lower-bound-only is permissive and idiomatic for libraries.

rule.statement: Set virtualenvs.in-project = true so .venv lives next to pyproject. IDEs and CI both discover it.
rule.rationale: Hidden venvs in ~/.cache/pypoetry break IDE auto-detection and confuse new contributors.

rule.statement: CI installs with `poetry install --sync --no-interaction`. A bare `poetry install` in CI is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: `--sync` removes packages that have left the lockfile. Without it a removed dependency stays resident in the cached venv and code importing it keeps passing CI — the build is green on a dependency that no longer exists in the manifest.

rule.statement: Never run `poetry update` with no arguments in a shared repo. Bump one package at a time: `poetry update <package>`.
rule.rationale: A bare update rewrites the whole lockfile, silently overwriting the resolution another developer or agent has staged, and produces a diff nobody can review. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Use a tight Python constraint (`python = "^3.11"` or newer), never a broad range like `>=3.8`.
rule.rationale: A broad range makes the solver explore versions nobody will ever run — roughly an order of magnitude slower — and turns any conflict into a cryptic message about a Python version the project never targeted. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Run `poetry check --lock` BEFORE any `poetry add` or `poetry remove`; resolve lockfile drift first.
rule.rationale: Adding a dependency on top of an already-drifted lockfile compounds the drift and buries the original cause inside a much larger diff.

rule.statement: In Docker, the builder stage runs `poetry export` and the final stage runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`. `poetry install` in the FINAL stage is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: Shipping the Poetry runtime into production adds 100-150MB and a dependency resolver to an image that only needs to run the app. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: CI uses `snok/install-poetry@v1` (or an equivalent pinned installer) and caches `.venv` keyed by OS + Python version + `poetry.lock` hash.
rule.rationale: The lockfile hash is the correct cache key because it changes exactly when the resolved set changes. On a hit this turns a multi-minute install into seconds; keyed on anything looser it silently serves a stale environment.
